steps.text: Mix buttermilk, vegetable oil, and vanilla in a bowl; stir in sugar. Whisk in flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt, combining the batter with just a few strokes to moisten. Leave the lumps.
Whisk egg and lemon juice together in a separate bowl; gently stir into the batter. Refrigerate the batter for at least 30 minutes, up to 1 hour.
Heat a large skillet over medium heat and grease with the butter. Pour 1/3 cup of batter per pancake into the skillet and cook until bubbles appear on the surface, about 2 minutes.
Flip with spatula and brown the other side, about 2 more minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: My-Hop Pancakes
raw_recipe.description: These delicious pancakes are said to resemble those from a famous pancake house. The batter rests in the refrigerator for 30 minutes, making the cakes extra fluffy.

review.reviewBody: Great pancake recipe! I didn't change a thing! There's nothing better on a Sunday morning than the smell of a home cooked breakfast and freshly brewed coffee. Be sure to use REAL buttermilk and don't over stir the batter. You'll get some really nice and fluffy pankcakes - perfect with real maple syrup or sliced strawberries and whipped cream!

Very easy and delicious. I prepared the batter the night before so I wouldn't need to let it rest in the morning. It became rather thick, but I just thinned it a bit with more milk. Oh, and I added cinnamon - because I love it! Froze the leftovers and toasted them the next day, yum. Recipe works very well for us two.

These are very good pancakes. If you read this I would caution you: the batter will seem a bit too think after mixing, but it loosens up very nicely after the rest. This gives it time for the leavening agents to do their job and for the flour to fully saturate with the liquid. I added blueberries to half of the pancakes, and this batter fluffed up perfectly around the berries. The flavor also paired well with some homemade whipped cream.

Thank you to the reviewer who suggested dropping blueberries onto the batter on the skillet. I always mixed them in before, and it's very difficult to get them evenly distributed, and they cooked strangely. 

The recipe was quite good, and although I pulled the buttermilk and egg out of the fridge for a few minutes, there was no waiting time for me today because my partner and I were already hungry. Ok, I let the batter sit a few minutes, and bubbles started to develop immediately. They still turned out much better than using another recipe and powdered buttermilk. Fresh buttermilk does seem to taste better and leaves a thicker consistency than water and powder.

Really the trickiest part of pancakes (besides resisting the urge to smooth out all those lumps in the batter) seems to be getting the right temperature on the pan to cook without blackening. I don't have a griddle so I'm using a stainless steel pan on a flat top glass electric range. 

Happy cooking, everyone!

Fabulous!!! As a general rule I don’t have the best luck with pancakes but today is my son’s birthday and he requested them for breakfast. I hadn’t planned ahead so I used the milk and lemon juice trick for the buttermilk. I whisked together the dry ingredients and wet ingredients (and sugar) and then mixed wet into dry until just combined. Since I was in a rush I didn’t notice until it was too late, it being a school day, that this recipe requires chilling so I just forged ahead and cooked them immediately. PERFECTION. I couldn’t be more pleased with these pancakes, and I’m so happy that I finally have a recipe that works for me!

The pancakes are on the sweet side but very yummy and the lemon juice puts them over the top. 

Didn't have buttermilk on hand so I used 1 tablespoon plus 1 teaspoon and filled it in a measuring cup. I then added enough milk to have a total of 1 1/4 cups of "buttermilk". 

I chilled the batter for 1 hour and baked 1/4 cup of batter for each pancake. I ended up with 11 pancakes.

Quick and easy with plenty of flavor. Didn't have buttermilk, so I doubled the amount of lemon juice. Didn't let it rest more than 5 minutes while the grill heated, and they were perfect. I scaled the recipe down to three servings and it made six medium sized pancakes, a perfect breakfast for two hungry people.

Awesome! These were excellent pancakes. I didn't have any buttermilk in the refrigerator, so I substituted milk + distilled vinegar which worked fine. I also added a dash of nutmeg and cinnamon, and added a touch of almond extract. They. Were. Amazing.

I’ve made these pancakes so many times and they are great! If I don’t have buttermilk, I just mix one tablespoon of apple cider vinegar into my milk and add it to the other ingredients after 5 minutes. They still come out really good that way.

I'm overly critical of pancakes and I judge everyone's pancakes to IHOPs' pancakes and I won't eat them, with that said, these were delicious! My adult daughter who is my worst critic, has no filter when it comes to cooking in this house. If the food is good she will let you know, and if it's nasty she will definitely express that and state "you shouldn't make that again because it's nasty" and will remind you how dissatisfying it was if you attempt to make it again. SHE LOVED THESE PANCAKES and so did I...yum yum yummy! 

I didn't have buttermilk so I used half and half without the vinegar, and I substituted the vegetable oil for real butter. The next time I make them I will not make any substitutions and use a griddle. Thank you!

FYI, she just yelled from the other room "Mom, these pancakes are really good", this is a winner!

Great method. I discovered too late that I was nearly out of all purpose flour so I used what I had - 1/4 c. all- purpose flour, 1/2 c. bread flour, and 1/2 c. whole wheat flour. I did everything else was exactly the same as in the recipe. My family and I loved them. Seeing that our whole wheat pancakes out this light and fluffy, I figure it's got the be the method, not so much the type of flour used so I'm saving this recipe to try again exactly as written when I have all-purpose flour in my pantry but will definitely make them again substituting 1/2 the flour with whole wheat.
I have made this recipe couple times and it is always good! The outcome is fluffy pancakes each time.
The batter was way too runny. The pancakes came out flat and not fluffy at all. Adding the egg and lemon juice at the end did nothing for the taste or texture of the pancake.

Used this recipe for waffles. I did add two table spoons of brown sugar, a teaspoon of cinnamon, and increased the vanilla to 1 teaspoon. Keeping the leftovers in the freezer to have on hand for my picky eater.
This is the worst recipe for pancakes. The pancakes are flavorless and don’t hold together. What a waste of ingredients.
Came out perfect and delicious! Did not change anything! No need to buy it from the grocery store anymore!
I'm an ihop pancake lover. These came out so close that the restaurant just lost a great customer. My entire family loves these pancakes.
Best pancakes ever! My kids would rather have these than go out to that famous pancake house. I didn't change a thing (except for doubling the recipe!)
Great recipe - delicious and as good as IHOP. Go to recipe for pancakes 😋
